items.title: The generic points of the complement of an affine open immersion have local rings of dimension at most one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an open subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme whose inclusion is affine, the local ring at a generic point of the complement has dimension at most one, and dimension exactly one if the open is dense or the point lies in its closure (statement lines 3449-3460). The counted proof is short and complete: it identifies the restriction of the open over the spectrum of the local ring with the punctured spectrum, uses the affineness hypothesis to make that restriction affine, applies the characterization of affine punctured spectra to bound the dimension, and in the closure case produces a specialization from a point of the open to the given point to exclude dimension zero (proof lines 3462-3482). It is H2: the identification, the affineness step and the closure argument are all carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard base change and point-specialization statements.
